title: After a Year of Delays, Yash's 'Toxic' Finally Plants Its Flag — August 26, IMAX, and a Female Cast Stacked to the Ceiling
excerpt: The Rocking Star vanished from screens after KGF 2. His grown-up fairy tale has been shuffled four times. Now the date is locked, the format is IMAX, and Nayanthara, Kiara Advani and Huma Qureshi are loading the guns.
body:
Some stars chase the next release. **Yash** disappeared. After **KGF: Chapter 2** detonated ₹859.7 crore in India alone and turned a Kannada gangster into a pan-Indian deity, the Rocking Star did the unthinkable: he went quiet. No quick cash-in. No franchise victory lap. Just a single, obsessively guarded project called **Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups** — and a release date that kept slipping through everyone's fingers like sand.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=aF08WVSvCok</youtube>

That date has finally been hammered into the ground. After a punishing run of postponements — March 19, then June 4, then a vague "globally aligned" shrug — *Toxic* is now locked for a worldwide theatrical release on **August 26, 2026**, and it is coming in IMAX. The wait, the teasing, the four false starts: over.


![Rocking Star — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/0/0c/Yash%2C_Vishal%2C_Srinidhi_Shetty_at_the_%E2%80%98KGF%E2%80%99_Press_Meet_In_Chennai_%28cropped%29.jpg)



> **"Toxic has been one such journey." — Yash

Let's talk about why the delays happened, because they reveal something about the ambition here."**



> "There are films we make, and then there are films that remind us why we fell in love with cinema. Toxic has been one such journey." — Yash

Let's talk about why the delays happened, because they reveal something about the ambition here. The film was originally meant to clash head-on with **Ranveer Singh's Dhurandhar 2** in March — a showdown trade analysts breathlessly dubbed the "Dhuroxic" battle. Then came regional instability in the Middle East. Then, after a rapturous reception at CinemaCon where international distributors lined up, the makers tore up their own plan and reached for something bigger. "Some stories ask for patience," Yash said. KVN Productions and his own Monster Mind Creations weren't delaying out of trouble — they were holding out for a genuinely global rollout. The IMAX confirmation, slotted into the format's official investor slate, is the proof.

And then there is the cast, which deserves a paragraph of its own. **Toxic** has assembled one of the most formidable female line-ups in modern Indian cinema, and the makers have leaned all the way in. South lady superstar **Nayanthara** makes what the posters call a "lethal entry" as Ganga, reportedly Yash's sister. **Kiara Advani** is Nadia, the female lead. **Tara Sutaria** plays the fierce Rebecca, **Huma Qureshi** is the primary antagonist Elizabeth, and **Rukmini Vasanth** rounds it out as the poised Mellisa. Industry insiders insist this isn't decorative casting — the women are integral to the protagonist's journey, a deliberate swerve away from the hero-worship template that films of this scale usually run on. For a movie built around the most worshipped male star in Sandalwood, that is a quietly radical choice.


![Fairy Tale — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/15/Carl_Larsson_-_Little_Red_Riding_Hood_1881.jpg/3840px-Carl_Larsson_-_Little_Red_Riding_Hood_1881.jpg)


Directing it all is **Geetu Mohandas**, the National Award-winning filmmaker who co-wrote the script with Yash. The music comes from **Ravi Basrur**, the composer whose thunderous KGF score became its own cultural event — this is his third collaboration with Yash — with additional work from Vishal Mishra, Tanishk Bagchi and others. The first single, *Tabaahi*, dropped on March 2 and did exactly what its title promised. The film's first-look glimpse, unveiled on Yash's 40th birthday in January, racked up over 200 million views and 5.5 million likes in 24 hours. The appetite is not in question.

Yash, for his part, has been refreshingly candid about why a finished film took so long to reach screens. He pointed to the gulf between Indian and Western release systems — in the West, films are locked and dated long before marketing begins, while Indian productions often sprint to the line. *Toxic* is complete. The delay was never about the cut; it was about the launchpad.

**For the diaspora, August 26 is a date worth circling now.** *Toxic* releases not just in Kannada and English but in Hindi, Telugu, Tamil and Malayalam — and with IMAX in the mix, NRIs in the US, UK, Canada and the Gulf can expect premium-format screens from day one rather than the usual second-week trickle. A Yash film, in your language, on the biggest screen your city offers, on a long-weekend-adjacent Wednesday: the makers know exactly who they are courting.

Four years after KGF 2, the most patient man in Indian cinema is about to find out if absence really does make the box office grow fonder. The smart money says the wait was the strategy all along.
